howEachStateWasAssigned.implemented-unverified: a web surface was traced from the desktop form to a registered route, a dynamic master name, or a page file, and that surface is machine-verified to resolve by apps/api/test/completionRegister.test.ts. Nothing proves it MATCHES the desktop, which is exactly what this state means.
howEachStateWasAssigned.absent: no defensible web surface was found. Recorded rather than hidden under a softer state.
howEachStateWasAssigned.verified: DELIBERATELY UNUSED. The register defines it as compared or tested, but the plan means desktop-verified, and the controlling comparison is 0 of 66 matched (project-memory/parity/g5). Claiming verified from web-only tests would be the self-approval this project keeps finding.
howEachStateWasAssigned.implemented-elsewhere: DELIBERATELY UNUSED. Every mapped entry here is reached through a web feature with a different name, so the label would apply to all 145 and distinguish nothing. The real signal — which entries collapse onto one shared surface — is recorded per item in sharedSurfaceWith instead.
howEachStateWasAssigned.dead-in-dataset: NOT USED. Requires Live24 row counts that were not available.
howEachStateWasAssigned.scope-excluded: NOT USED. Requires an owner decision (plan §8.1); a classifier cannot exclude scope on the business owner’s behalf.

method.rejectedMethods: Label matching reported 165 of 198 missing including Sales and Purchase; table-name grepping reported a hit for almost everything. Each entry was instead traced desktop form -> web implementation -> the exact registration site.
method.whatThisDoesNotEstablish: that any mapped surface behaves like the desktop. Modes are the known risk: 52 entries share 21 surfaces, and at least one collapsed pair is only half implemented (ExtraTran/Other Expenses is mapped while ExtraTran/Other Income is absent). WP-05 contracts must resolve each shared surface mode by mode.
